raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Every engine core and worker process imports `vllm.v1.structured_output` (through `vllm.v1.request`). It imported `ParserEngineReasoningAdapter` at module level only for two `isinstance` checks, and that import pulls in `vllm.parser` and with it `openai`, `fastapi`, `starlette` and the `vllm.entrypoints` protocol modules. This is the "EngineCore imports fastapi and the openai protocol types through v1.request → structured_output → parser → entrypoints.*.protocol" item in #59433, and a follow-up to #65423. This PR checks the class through `sys.modules` instead, so nothing is imported.

## Claims

- After `import vllm.v1.engine.core`, `openai`, `fastapi`, `starlette`, `vllm.entrypoints` and `vllm.parser` modules are no longer loaded (counts below). The same holds for `vllm.v1.worker.gpu_worker` and `vllm.v1.executor.multiproc_executor`.
- No import happens at runtime either: if `vllm.parser.engine.adapters` was never imported, no adapter instance can exist, so the check is a dict lookup.
- Scope: this is import-time. When `--reasoning-parser` is set, `StructuredOutputManager.__init__` still loads the parser (and, for non-engine parsers, the protocol modules) at engine start. So the runtime saving applies to engines without a reasoning parser.

## Validation

```bash
python3 tests/standalone_tests/lazy_imports.py
pytest tests/v1/structured_output/ tests/v1/spec_decode/test_mtp_structured_output.py tests/reasoning/
```

```text
# main
  File "tests/standalone_tests/lazy_imports.py", line 26, in <module>
  File "vllm/v1/structured_output/__init__.py", line 14, in <module>
  File "vllm/parser/abstract_parser.py", line 10, in <module>
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'openai.types'; 'openai' is not a package
exit 1

# this PR
exit 0
```

Modules loaded after `import vllm.v1.engine.core`:

| | openai | fastapi | starlette | vllm.entrypoints | vllm.parser | total |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| CUDA, main | 522 | 38 | 21 | 17 | 10 | 5530 |
| CUDA, this PR | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 4855 |
| CPU, main | 522 | 38 | 21 | 17 | 10 | 4797 |
| CPU, this PR | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 4122 |

CUDA is 1x NVIDIA B300 with vLLM nightly `76c6f3f2a`, with #65423 and this PR applied (the touched file is identical to this branch's base); `lazy_imports.py` also passes there. CPU is macOS with `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu`. `-X importtime` for `import vllm.v1.engine.core` on CPU: 5.82 s → 5.35 s (median of 3).

Tests on CPU: 761 passed on main and with this PR. The same 2 tests fail on both (`test_backend_xgrammar.py::TestXgrammarBackend::TestPR58067Regressions::test_disable_any_whitespace_is_{false,true}`, a fixture-discovery error unrelated to this change). `ruff check`, `ruff format --check` and `pre-commit run --files` (including mypy) pass on the changed files.

## Details

- `_is_parser_engine_reasoner` returns `TypeIs[ParserEngineReasoningAdapter]`, following `vllm/model_executor/models/interfaces.py`, so the call sites keep their narrowing.
- A function-local import would also work, but this helper runs inside `grammar_bitmask` in the scheduler step. With a non-engine reasoning parser, the first structured-output request would then pay for importing `vllm.parser` (~110 ms on CPU) inside one scheduling step. The `sys.modules` check avoids that.
- The test imports `vllm.v1.structured_output` under the existing `openai` block. `vllm.v1.engine.core` can't be used there yet, because `vllm.utils.deep_gemm` still imports `torch._inductor.async_compile`; a separate PR addresses that.
- CI: `lazy_imports.py` currently runs only in the `(CPU) Params, Env, Tokenizers, Parser` job, which is commented out in `.buildkite/test_areas/misc.yaml` (#63609). #64414 restores it.
- Not a duplicate: no open PR changes this import. #57310 and my deep_gemm PR also edit the end of `lazy_imports.py`, so whichever lands later needs a trivial rebase.

AI assistance: Claude Code was used to draft the change, the test and this description. I reviewed the changes, the measurements and the test results before submitting.

 module_names = ["torch._inductor.async_compile", "cv2", "openai"]
 
 # set all modules in `module_names` to be None.

 else:
@@ -36,6 +38,17 @@
 logger = init_logger(__name__)
 
 
+def _is_parser_engine_reasoner(
+    reasoner: "ReasoningParser | None",
+) -> "TypeIs[ParserEngineReasoningAdapter]":
+    # Not imported here: `vllm.parser` pulls in openai and the HTTP layer.
+    # If the module was never loaded, no adapter instance can exist.
+    adapters = sys.modules.get("vllm.parser.engine.adapters")
+    return adapters is not None and isinstance(
+        reasoner, adapters.ParserEngineReasoningAdapter
+    )
+

 class ConstraintBounds(NamedTuple):

-            if isinstance(reasoner, ParserEngineReasoningAdapter):
+            if _is_parser_engine_reasoner(reasoner):
                 grammar = structured_req.grammar
                 assert isinstance(grammar, StructuredOutputGrammar)
                 masked = tuple(
@@ -324,10 +337,7 @@ def _get_constraint_bounds(
             return _NO_SPEC_TOKENS
 
         # Engine-based parsers also report whether the end token is content.
-        if (
-            isinstance(reasoner, ParserEngineReasoningAdapter)
-            and reasoner.reasoning_end_token_ids
-        ):
+        if _is_parser_engine_reasoner(reasoner) and reasoner.reasoning_end_token_ids:
             end = reasoner.find_reasoning_end(spec_tokens)
             if end is not None:
                 constraint_start = end.offset + 1
